answer: Deposits are visible in beacon, and ivory reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 20% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 145 aliases, and each one needs its own funded onyx account. Scaling to 664 identities multiplies that fee by 664 with no matching gain in influence. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
